_comment: Tier-2 for axisymmetric:3 and :5. axisymmetric:3 — 'global weight cell radius' has two ordering constraints with two DIFFERENT messages, both matched verbatim: 'ERROR: Cannot use weight cell radius unless axisymmetric (../grid.cpp:1997)' when the boundary is not 'ar', and 'ERROR: Cannot weight cells before grid is defined (../grid.cpp:1983)' when it precedes create_grid; boundary-then-grid-then-weight runs. axisymmetric:5 — the 'Axisymm bad moves = 0' line is printed by all three completed runs INCLUDING the plain 'boundary o o p' non-axisymmetric one, which is the entry's point: presence carries no information, only a nonzero value does. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 with SPARTA (24 Sep 2025). ATTRIBUTION: axisymmetric:3 is executed here too, but it is also executed by the older axisymmetric_boundary_letter_forms fixture, so it is counted there and this fixture claims only axisymmetric:5. Double-counting one claim across two fixtures would inflate the coverage fraction. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 fixes the ORDERING in both wrong decks — the non-axisymmetric one gets 'boundary o ar p', and the one that weighted before create_grid weights after it — so both become the deck this fixture already runs as the correct order, and nothing else changes. Both then exit rc=0 with an empty error list instead of aborting at grid.cpp:1997 and grid.cpp:1983. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and this expect_in_output string goes False and disappears: both_quoted_weight_radius_messages_are_verbatim=True; the run also prints two 'UNEXPECTED: ... printed [] not ...' lines, which trip forbid_in_output. LIMIT OF THE CONTROL, stated plainly: only the axisymmetric:3 half is covered. The axisymmetric:5 half cannot be mutation-controlled from a deck at all, because its claim is about SPARTA's own output — that 'Axisymm bad moves = 0' is printed by every completed run, axisymmetric or not — so no edit to any deck removes that pathology; only a change to SPARTA would. axisymm_bad_moves_line_appears_in_every_completed_run, it_appears_even_in_a_non_axisymmetric_run and so_only_a_nonzero_value_carries_information all stay True under T2_MUTATE=1 and are NOT evidenced by this hook. Note also that the_two_ordering_constraints_have_different_messages compares two string literals defined in source.py and is therefore True by construction; what makes it meaningful is the companion both_quoted_weight_radius_messages_are_verbatim, which requires the binary to have printed both of those literals. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/axisymmetric_weight_radius_and_bad_moves && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line. FIXED 2026-08-08 (assertion changed): the_two_ordering_constraints_have_different_messages was QUOTED['weight_radius_on_a_non_axisymmetric_model'] != QUOTED['weight_radius_before_create_grid'] -- both operands are the string constants defined thirty lines above in source.py, so the line asserted that the author typed two different strings. It could not come out False on any SPARTA version, with or without the pathology, and the name claims a fact about SPARTA's diagnostics. It now compares the two messages SPARTA ACTUALLY PRINTED, which are also printed as observed_* so the comparison can be read. Measured 2026-08-08: observed_non_axisymmetric_message=['ERROR: Cannot use weight cell radius unless axisymmetric (../grid.cpp:1997)'], observed_before_create_grid_message=['ERROR: Cannot weight cells before grid is defined (../grid.cpp:1983)'], flag True, rc=0. T2_MUTATE=1, executed: both decks are written in the correct order, both observed messages are [], the flag is False and rc=1 -- so the line now dies with the pathology where before it survived it. The old form is literally the tautology control: it compares two module constants, so under that same mutated run it would have printed True beside two empty observed messages.
